rename.resolution: `QoS::lifespan(const nros::Duration&)` / `QoS::lifespan()` shipped 2026-08-27 and MATCHES rclcpp; the `_ms` pair remains as [[deprecated]] forwarders pending removal. The blocking dependency (`cpp:Duration`) was satisfied 2026-08-25 by issue 0789.

retired: deleted by phase-482 W6 with every other deprecated item; the row records the rename
why:
LANDED 2026-08-27 (phase-379 W5). The four policy enums are now PUBLIC and at NAMESPACE scope under rclcpp's names (`nros::ReliabilityPolicy`, `nros::DurabilityPolicy`, `nros::HistoryPolicy`, `nros::LivelinessPolicy`, `packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/qos.hpp`), the getters return them (`reliability()` / `durability()` / `history()` / `liveliness()`), and the three time windows take and return `nros::Duration` (`deadline()` / `lifespan()` / `liveliness_lease_duration()`). Their theirs-only rows are gone because those items MATCH now. This row is now the DEPRECATED ALIAS pair (`QoS::lifespan_ms(uint32_t)` and `QoS::lifespan_ms()`). STALE PREMISE CORRECTED: the old text said the `_ms` suffix existed because "C++ has NO `Duration` type here" and that the name had to follow whatever W3 decided about `cpp:Duration`. Both died on 2026-08-25, when `nros::Duration` shipped (issue 0789, `packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/duration.hpp`, exported by `rclcpp/rclcpp.hpp`); the cross-reference `cpp:Duration::Duration` names a key that exists in no shard. The live spelling is `QoS::lifespan(const nros::Duration&)` / `QoS::lifespan()`. THE C ABI DID NOT MOVE: `nros_cpp_qos_t.lifespan_ms` is still `uint32_t` milliseconds, as are its mirrors in `nros_cpp_ffi.h` and `rclc/component.h` -- the same token is a struct FIELD (ABI) and was a class METHOD (renamed), and only the method moved. `nros::Duration` -> milliseconds is a boundary conversion with a documented rule (`detail::qos_window_ms`): non-positive -> `0`, which is the ABI's INFINITE; otherwise ROUND UP, so a sub-millisecond window becomes 1 ms rather than silently becoming infinite; above `UINT32_MAX` ms it saturates. It survives as a `[[deprecated]]` inline member, so a stale caller still compiles and is told what to write instead -- verified under `-Werror=deprecated-declarations` by `qos_deprecation_probe.cpp`, which `just check cpp` required to FAIL until phase-482 W6 deleted it with the member. Header-inline templates, so this costs no ABI: no exported symbol changed. Removal is the follow-up the maintainer asked for ("we'll retire deprecated items later"), and this row is where the deprecation is recorded, on the `c:param_declare_*` precedent from the C half of the same week.

RETIRED by phase-482 W6 (2026-10-07): the deprecated item is DELETED, with every other deprecated item in the tree as one batch (changelog.d/+phase-482-w6.breaking.md). Code that still names it gets an undeclared-identifier error naming nothing; the changelog entry carries the replacement. The row is kept as the record of the rename.
